title: fix: compaction aborts a slow summary request that is still streaming
body:
Related: #130971

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: compaction aborts a healthy summary request that is still streaming output, because the timeout window (`agents.defaults.compaction.timeoutSeconds`, 180 s default) caps each request's total duration instead of its silence. On a large session or a slower model the user sees "⚠️ This conversation is too long, and shortening it took too long." while the model was still writing the summary.

## User Impact

User impact: large sessions compact even when a single summary request runs longer than `timeoutSeconds`, as long as it keeps streaming. A request that goes silent is still aborted one window after its last output, so a hung provider still fails at about the same time as before. No new config keys, messages, or warnings; the timeout error and its user-facing text are unchanged.

New bound: the whole compaction stops after 10 windows (30 minutes at the default) even if output keeps trickling. Built-in compaction had no operation-level ceiling on `main` once #130993 made every request start a fresh window; plugin-owned compaction keeps its one-window bound.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Root cause.** The host compaction watchdog is refreshed only at request boundaries: after setup, when each provider request starts (`onStarted` in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compaction-session-execution.ts:343-348` on `main`), and after success or before a thinking fallback. Nothing refreshes it while a request streams, so a single request is bounded by `timeoutSeconds` from its start no matter how much output it produces.

**Provenance.** #130993 (a93a015a5695) introduced the per-request refresh ("keep staged compaction progress alive") and kept plugin compaction "bounded once at the host boundary". #163636 (02ec714206d) moved the refresh capability onto the operation's composed abort signal (`compactionWatchdogResets`) so delegating plugins get it too. Both left single-request progress open, as noted in the issue thread. Both invariants are kept here. #164246 (c0c6ca35fce, merged after this PR opened) made an automatic compaction whose summary times out commit a deterministic reduction instead of failing; this PR keeps that outcome reachable at the new ceiling (see *Summary cutoff*).

**Fix.**
- *Progress = a streamed model output delta.* The compaction diagnostic stream wrapper already sees every provider event. It now calls a new `onOutputDelta` callback for each non-empty `text_delta`, `thinking_delta` or `toolcall_delta` (`attempt.model-diagnostic-lifecycle.ts`). Compaction wires it to the same refresh as `onStarted`, which resets both the native and delegated watchdogs. These are parsed provider events, not raw bytes: SSE keepalives, `response.in_progress`-style frames, structural `*_start`/`*_end` events, empty deltas and loop ticks never count (the point from the issue's idleDeadline/totalDeadline comment). Reasoning deltas count because the model is producing output; a provider that hangs produces none.
- *Ceiling.* `runAbortableTimeout` takes an optional `maxTotalMs`: each reset arms `min(timeoutMs, deadline - now)` (never below 0), and resets at or after the deadline leave the due timer alone. The host watchdog (`compactContextEngineWithSafetyTimeout`) fixes its ceiling at `10 × timeoutMs` from the operation start, so there is no new config key. It is derived from the existing knob: raising `timeoutSeconds` raises both. At the default that is 30 minutes: 5.5× the 327 s this 963k-token session's compaction took in run 2 below, and 3.4× the slowest earlier measurement of a similar session (527 s, #163636).
- *Summary cutoff.* The host registers `{ reset, deadlineAt }` for its signal (`compactionWatchdogs`, replacing the reset-only `compactionWatchdogResets`), and `delegateCompactionToRuntime` forwards both. The native summary watchdog ends one window before the host ceiling, so a summary still streaming at the ceiling times out on its own watchdog: an automatic compaction commits #164246's deterministic reduction inside the reserved window, and manual `/compact` keeps failing with "Compaction timed out". Without this, the host deadline fired first (it starts before the summary), aborted the caller signal, and the automatic fallback was skipped (found by the post-rebase review). Direct compaction without a host keeps its own 10-window ceiling.
- *Plugin work stays bounded once.* Only the runtime delegate's model requests refresh the host window. Plugin code before or after delegating, and engines that never delegate, still get one window. The #163636 test "keeps plugin-owned work after the delegate under one host window" and the #130993 test "threads timeout cancellation into the plugin compactor" are unchanged and pass.
- *Same model everywhere.* Manual `/compact`, `sessions.compact` and preflight/overflow/timeout recovery all enter through `compactContextEngineWithSafetyTimeout`. When they reach built-in compaction, they share the runtime delegate, the native watchdog and the same wrapped stream. #133260 (Stop honored) and #159105 (run timeout stops recovery) are untouched: caller cancellation still aborts the composed signal immediately.

## Evidence

**Regression through the real path** (`compact.hooks.test.ts` › "progress-aware compaction watchdog"). The chain is real: `compactEmbeddedAgentSession` → host watchdog → context engine → real `delegateCompactionToRuntime` → native watchdog → real `AgentSession` → core summarizer → diagnostic stream wrapper. Only the provider stream is scripted (one text delta every 20 s, 30 s window, 300 s ceiling).

| case | origin/main b2bdae9f046 | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| streams 220 s, longer than the window | **fail:** `{ ok: false, reason: "Compaction timed out" }` at 30 s | compacts |
| last delta at 100 s, then silent | **fail:** settled at 30 s, before the idle deadline | fails at exactly 130 s with "Compaction timed out" |
| last delta at 100 s, then empty-delta keepalives | **fail:** settled at 30 s | fails at exactly 130 s (keepalives don't extend it) |
| delta every 20 s forever, 5 s setup (manual) | **fail:** settled at 30 s | fails at exactly 270 s, one window before the 300 s ceiling; the last delta (265 s) leaves less than a window |
| automatic compaction, last delta at 100 s then silent | n/a | idle window fires; #164246's deterministic reduction is committed (`ok: true, compacted: true`) |
| automatic compaction, delta every 20 s forever, 5 s setup | n/a | summary cutoff at 270 s; deterministic reduction committed. At ea03e21 (before the cutoff) this case returned `{ ok: false, compacted: false }` |

The trickle cadence is chosen so the last delta before the cutoff leaves less than one window: a revision that ignored refreshes near the deadline instead of clamping them would fail the manual case at 255 s. `with-timeout.test.ts` adds that an already-passed deadline times out immediately without Node's `TimeoutNegativeWarning` (fails without the clamp).

Focused suites pass on the rebased head (the final commit only touched `with-timeout`, rerun there): `compact.hooks.test.ts` (94), `compact.summary-fallback.test.ts` (8), `delegate-watchdog.test.ts` (5), `embedded-agent-runner.compaction-safety-timeout.test.ts`, `with-timeout.test.ts` (4), `attempt.model-diagnostic-events.test.ts`, `attempt.model-diagnostic-lifecycle.test.ts`, `run.compaction-runtime.test.ts`, `run.recovery-deadline.test.ts`, `run.overflow-compaction.test.ts`, `compact.queued-successor.test.ts`, `context-engine-lifecycle.test.ts`. Also `pnpm tsgo:core`, oxlint/oxfmt on the changed files, and `pnpm config:docs:check`.

### Live: Telegram Test Server, real `gpt-6-astra`

Setup: real-user DM on the Telegram Test Server, built `dist` of each head, default context engine, compaction mode as shipped. Every model request goes through a forwarding proxy in front of the OpenAI API. In runs 1–3 it only records timing: per-request duration, first/last output-delta time, and the largest gap between deltas as forwarded to the gateway. Every run uses the same synthetic 1,250-message seed (3.8M chars; estimator 963k tokens vs the 902k threshold), so the next DM triggers preflight compaction.

**1. Before/after at `timeoutSeconds: 60`** (the live model's natural request length is 45–85 s, so this reproduces a request outliving its window without injecting anything):

| | origin/main b2bdae9f046 | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| compaction | `outcome=failed reason=timeout durationMs=110758` | `outcome=compacted durationMs=301232`, one attempt |
| user saw | "⚠️ This conversation is too long, and shortening it took too long. Try again, use /compact, or use /new to start a fresh session." | a normal answer to the question |

Per compaction request (ms; gap = longest silence between forwarded output deltas):

| stage | before: duration / first delta / max gap | after: duration / first delta / max gap |
| --- | --- | --- |
| chunk 1 summarize (254k in) | 50,311 / 7,668 / 314 | 43,589 / 5,575 / 217 |
| chunk 1 update (136k in) | **60,000 aborted** while streaming: last delta at 59,989, max gap 152 | 57,662 / 5,689 / 215 |
| chunk 2 summarize (255k in) | – | 50,885 / 10,958 / 207 |
| chunk 2 update (139k in) | – | **60,772** / 5,227 / 344 |
| merge (12k in, 8.3k out) | – | **83,309** / 4,686 / 204 |
| follow-up summarize | – | 4,399 / 1,457 / 134 |

Before: the update request was still streaming 11 ms before the watchdog killed it at exactly 60.0 s. After: two requests ran past the 60 s window (60.8 s, 83.3 s) without ever being silent for more than 344 ms, and compaction finished in one attempt.

**2. Default `timeoutSeconds` (unset → 180 s), this PR at 82bf344628:** compaction `outcome=compacted durationMs=326671` in one attempt (6 serial requests, no retries, no timeout lines). The user got a normal answer to the question 334 s after sending it.

| stage | duration / first delta / max gap (ms) |
| --- | --- |
| chunk 1 summarize (254k in) | 46,024 / 4,721 / 632 |
| chunk 1 update (136k in) | 63,671 / 6,026 / 282 |
| chunk 2 summarize (255k in) | 51,736 / 5,854 / 342 |
| chunk 2 update (139k in) | 64,837 / 5,107 / 327 |
| merge (12k in, 9.0k out) | 96,317 / 6,967 / 349 |
| follow-up summarize | 3,529 / 1,266 / 80 |

**3. Forced mid-stream stall, default window, this PR at 82bf344628.** The live model can't be made to stall on demand, so for the first compaction request the proxy forwards real `gpt-6-astra` output until 40 output deltas reach the gateway (6.25 s in). It then stops forwarding and cancels upstream while holding the gateway's socket open and silent. Result: the gateway closed the request **180.003 s after the last forwarded delta** (186.3 s after it started), compaction ended `outcome=failed reason=timeout durationMs=186742` (`Compaction timed out`), and the user got the existing timeout message ("⚠️ This conversation is too long, and shortening it took too long. …"). The stall failed at the idle window, not at the 30-minute ceiling, and no new text appeared.

Proof artifacts (local): proxy NDJSON per request, gateway log, and the Telegram event timeline for each run. The forwarding proxies never log the API key or request/response bodies.

### Rebased head 5532d8e8eb re-run (Telegram Test Server, real `gpt-6-astra`)

Rebase onto current main, provenance decisions:
- `compaction-safety-timeout.ts`: main replaced the local `raceCompactionWithAbortSignal` with the shared `racePromiseWithAbortSignal` (caller-cancel error mapping). Kept main's helper and error mapping; the PR's ceiling-clamped reset now runs inside it. No behavior change to the PR.
- `compact.hooks.test.ts`: #164768 retired the `createAgentSessionForEmbeddedRunner` SDK export in favor of `createAgentSession`; the PR's test now mocks `createAgentSession`.
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256`: regenerated on the new base.

Same harness and 963k-token seed as above, built `dist` at `5532d8e8eb`, default `timeoutSeconds`:

| Scenario | Outcome | Artifact |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Large session, default settings | `outcome=compacted durationMs=387436`, one attempt, 6 compaction requests; user got a normal two-sentence answer | `dcw-live/idle/rebased-default` |
| Forced mid-stream stall (proxy stops forwarding after 40 real deltas, 12.9 s in) | gateway closed the request **180.005 s after the last delta**; `outcome=failed reason=timeout durationMs=193339`; user got the existing "⚠️ This conversation is too long, and shortening it took too long. …" text, nothing new | `dcw-live/idle/rebased-stall` |
| Plugin-delegating context engine (`delegating-probe`, ~2 s plugin work then `delegateCompactionToRuntime`) | `outcome=compacted durationMs=361406`, one attempt; user got a normal answer | `dcw-live/idle/rebased-plugin` |

The live proof above remains valid: the rebase did not change the PR's behavior, and these runs confirm it on the exact head.

### Rebased head d1e38859e7 onto main with #164246 (Telegram Test Server, real `gpt-6-astra`)

Rebase provenance:
- `compact.hooks.test.ts` conflicted after #164246 (c0c6ca35fce) and its neighbor rewrote the adjacent "plans direct compaction with the admitted workspace manifest policy" test into the `plans canonical fallback plugins from the $source` `it.each`. Kept main's `it.each` unchanged and inserted this PR's `describe` before it. `compaction-session-execution.ts` auto-merged with #164246's fallback path.
- Semantic interaction (not a textual conflict): #164246 decided that an automatic compaction whose summary times out commits a deterministic reduction. This PR's host ceiling fired before the summary watchdog and skipped that path. Adapted the PR to main's decision with the *Summary cutoff* above (commits 93f65f4a1b, d1e38859e7); main's behavior is unchanged.

Same harness and 963k-token seed, built `dist` of each head:

| Scenario | ea03e21ff3 (rebased, before the cutoff) | d1e38859e7 (this head) | Artifact |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `timeoutSeconds: 30` (ceiling 300 s), summary still streaming at the ceiling | merge request aborted **32.3 s in, 41 ms after its last delta**; `trigger=budget outcome=failed reason=timeout durationMs=299983`; user got "⚠️ This conversation is too long, and shortening it took too long. …" | summary cut at the cutoff (merge request 27.8 s in, still streaming); `[compaction-diag] fallback … reason=timeout summary=deterministic`, `outcome=compacted reason=timeout summary=deterministic durationMs=269874`; user got a normal two-sentence answer | `dcw-live/idle/r2-before-ceiling30`, `r2-after-ceiling30` |
| Large session, default settings | – | `outcome=compacted reason=none durationMs=334793`, one attempt, 6 compaction requests (longest 77.9 s, max delta gap 474 ms); normal answer | `dcw-live/idle/r2-default` |
| Forced mid-stream stall (proxy stops forwarding after 40 real deltas, 5.7 s in) | – | gateway closed the request **180.005 s after the last delta**; with #164246 on main this automatic compaction now commits the deterministic reduction (`outcome=compacted reason=timeout summary=deterministic durationMs=185978`) and the user got a normal answer instead of the timeout text | `dcw-live/idle/r2-stall` |
| Plugin-delegating context engine (`delegating-probe`, ~2 s plugin work then `delegateCompactionToRuntime`) | – | `outcome=compacted reason=none durationMs=321600`, one attempt; normal answer | `dcw-live/idle/r2-plugin` |

No `TimeoutNegativeWarning` or other new warning lines in any gateway log; no new user-visible text.

## Compatibility

`agents.defaults.compaction.timeoutSeconds` changes meaning. On `main` it is the duration of each built-in compaction model request, restarted when the next serial request begins. With this PR it is how long a request may go **without progress**, where progress means a request start or a non-empty streamed text, reasoning or tool-call delta. Keepalives and empty deltas don't count. It also sets a new **operation ceiling of 10 × timeoutSeconds** (30 minutes at the default 180 s) on built-in compaction, which `main` didn't have.

- Who notices: a built-in compaction that keeps making progress for more than 10 windows now stops: the summary request ends one window before the ceiling, an automatic compaction then commits #164246's deterministic reduction, and manual `/compact` fails with the existing "Compaction timed out". The measured runs are well inside that: 327 s (1.8 windows) for the 963k-token session in run 2 above, and 527 s (2.9 windows) for the slowest similar run measured in #163636.
- What to do: raise `timeoutSeconds`. That raises both the idle window and the ceiling. No config migration is needed, and existing values stay valid.
- Unchanged: plugin-owned compaction work keeps one window for the complete operation, a request that is silent from the start fails at the same time as on `main`, and caller Stop or a run timeout still cancels immediately.
- Docs: the `timeoutSeconds` entries in `docs/gateway/config-agents/heartbeat-compaction-and-streaming.md` and the config help text describe the new semantics and the ceiling.

Maintainer decision recorded: keep the idle semantics with the 10-window operation ceiling (option A). The alternative, a per-request cap with no operation ceiling, was rejected because it drops the absolute bound the issue asked for (`totalDeadline`).

## Bounded cost

- Production (vs merge base): +83 / −24 across 8 files (the summary cutoff added the `compactionWatchdogs` deadline, its forwarding in `delegate.ts`, one internal param and the zero clamp). Tests +205 (one `describe` with 6 cases sharing one fixture, plus one `with-timeout` case). Docs and help: 2 lines plus the regenerated config hash.
- Runtime: one type/`length` check per streamed provider event on compaction requests, plus a `clearTimeout`/`setTimeout` pair per output delta. Normal agent turns pass no `onOutputDelta`, so they skip the check. No new timers, retries, config keys, SDK exports, warnings or messages.
- Worst-case deadline: a silent request dies one window after its last output (same as `main` when it is silent from the start). Any built-in compaction stops at 10 windows; under a host the summary stops at 9, leaving one window to commit. Plugin-owned work keeps one window.
- Live proof spend: about 2.4M input and 65k output `gpt-6-astra` tokens across the first four runs; about 3.4M input and 88k output across the five runs on the rebased heads (aborted requests report no usage and are not counted).

## Not changed

- Retry policy after a stall. The deterministic fallback itself is #164246 (landed); this PR only keeps it reachable at the ceiling.
- Chunk sizes, default `timeoutSeconds`, server-side Responses compaction (`server-endpoint-compaction.ts` keeps its own single-request window), the Codex app-server and Copilot harness compaction paths.
